query: I am covering Wrenfall next Saturday. Explain whom it serves, who keeps it running, and the boundaries I must explain to somebody bringing a donation.
For Wrenfall, why should a volunteer refuse a damp packet even when the donor says the crop is good, and what must the label establish before it goes in the drawer?
Can Wrenfall accept a crate of ornamental bulbs now, or does the donor need a different arrangement?
Before the drawer inspection, what Wrenfall labeling requirement and opening date were envisaged?
A colleague has offered to help with Patchbay. Give them the point of the collection, the person responsible, and what a member of the public can actually do with a recording.
When Patchbay receives an interview recorder, what protects the original during cataloguing, and why would a verified copy still not be ready for a public website?
Who approved the public Patchbay audio trailer, and can the drafted media file be treated as their authorization?
Why does Patchbay require an appointment in the history room instead of letting a visitor download a short extract?
Tomorrow is my first Millrace shift: set out the community benefit, the coordinator, and the limit of a volunteer's authority when the river appears to rise.
Why is a dramatic Millrace camera picture insufficient to send a checked threshold alert, and what confirmation is required instead?
For Millrace, tell the outgoing pair what the next shift needs in the written log and why sending that log does not give volunteers control of the siren.
Does the Millrace automation idea supersede the checked escalation process, and may the watch activate the town siren?
I found a rota card labeled Relay. Does that name alone tell me whether to use the recording procedure or the river-watch procedure?
Who should I contact for Patchbay and Millrace respectively, and what different community work is each person looking after?
